real_objective: Determine, per runnable public bar, whether a pinned donor-independent generator exists at zero spend and how large the remaining capability gap is, so the shortest verified path to a first real predicate can be named.
governing_invariants: Hard $0 incremental spend unless the owner records an explicit exception.
Models may be a substrate only if the Brain-owned configuration materially adds the capability (General Cognition Substrate Law V3); a substrate alone earns no ownership credit.
No untouched or frozen qualification case may be exposed to measure route quality; route quality is estimated on non-frozen development tasks.
Unknown, unpinned or unverified route facts fail closed.

material_premises.fact: On Cognition's own FrontierCode 1.1 Main leaderboard the best Workers-AI-available open-weights row is GLM 5.3 (max) at 40.1% (others: Kimi K2.7 30.1%, DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 28.5%, DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 18.8%) against Opus 5.5 (medium) at 54.6%; the registry bar is 54.4%. Residual a Brain-owned configuration must supply over the best such baseline: about 14.3 points.

On Artificial Analysis's Terminal-Bench 4.0 board (mini-SWE-agent harness, 66 tasks) the best open-weights row is GLM-5.3 at 41.8% against a 70.6% leader; the registry bar is 66.4%. Residual: about 24.6 points under that harness. Harness effects on the same model were not established here.

Ante's published open-weights scores (for example 83.9% for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) are Terminal-Bench 2.1 (89 tasks, a different and relaxed benchmark) and are deliberately NOT used as Terminal-Bench 4.0 evidence. They do show that the same family of open models scores far higher on the older benchmark with a strong harness, which is why a measured uplift protocol on non-frozen tasks is worth specifying.

Workers AI text generation is limited to 300 requests per minute by default, but any model that requires the Workers Paid plan is limited to 20 requests per minute per account per model (50 with prepaid AI Gateway credits); Cloudflare states these limits are designed for typical agentic and coding workloads. At 20 requests/minute a pass of about 5,000 to 5,700 requests (91 tasks x 52..63 median turns, the AA-Briefcase scale) takes roughly 4 to 5 hours, so the rate limit is not the binding constraint; the budget is. Which of the candidate model IDs require Workers Paid is stated on per-model pages that were not read.

material_premises.fact: A paired uplift experiment on the 89 name-disjoint Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks (raw pinned substrate versus Brain-configured system, same tasks) has, under a normal approximation with task-level clustering, a 95% CI half-width of about 6 to 10 points and about 92%+ power to detect the 14.3-point FrontierCode-sized residual when the per-task paired SD is at most 0.4. Estimated budget for 3 to 5 trials per task per arm (534 to 890 trials) is $23 to $10,720 across the two candidate models, two token mixes and a 0.57M to 10.7M tokens-per-trial proxy range (derived from AA-Briefcase per-task token usage). The spread is dominated by the unknown tokens per trial (about 19x), so a micro-pilot of 12 trials, costing about $0.51 to $40.29 at DeepSeek V4 Flash prices, should measure tokens per trial and per-task variance before the full experiment is sized. These are planning estimates with explicit assumptions, not measurements.

assumptions: Tasks are independent clusters; the outcome of interest is the per-task paired difference of success rates.
The SD of per-task paired differences is assumed (0.30, 0.40, 0.50), not measured.
Tokens per trial are proxied from AA-Briefcase (52M..970M tokens over 91 tasks); Terminal-Bench trials may differ by an unknown factor.
Prices as in P6; excludes retries, a Workers Paid base fee and any debugging spend.
evidence.decision_rule_proposal: Proceed to frozen runs only if the lower 95% bound of the measured uplift is at least the residual in P7 (FrontierCode) or P8 (TB4) for the surface being targeted; otherwise record the predicate as unattainable on this substrate.

DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (65.5) is just below the bar. For this surface the capability gap of the best Workers-AI-hosted open model is negative (about +7 points above the bar), unlike the agentic surfaces in P7 and P8.

The snapshot's release date was not recorded; the registry pins the bar to the 2026-06-25 release, so cross-release comparison is invalid until the same release is confirmed.

The Opus 5.5 row and the open rows are measured by the same leaderboard, but effort settings differ by row.

material_premises.ownership_caveat: A raw open model that already exceeds the bar would be an 'external capability provider' under General Cognition Substrate Law V3 unless the Brain-owned operative configuration measurably adds value (ablation: configuration versus bare 'use model X'). A passing score would still close the atomic public-bar predicate; family promotion and ownership credit have separate tests.

material_premises.fact: A LiveBench IF pass is small: questions average about 1800 input tokens (LiveBench paper, IF tasks summarize, paraphrase, story generation, simplify) and a few hundred output tokens without reasoning. For the three Workers-AI-hosted models above the bar, one pass of 50 to 200 questions costs 8,045 to 445,818 neurons (0.8 to 44.6 days of the 10,000-neuron/day free allocation, or $0.09 to $4.90 at the paid rate). The high end assumes 5,000 output tokens per question (reasoning models; GLM-5.3 reasoning cannot be disabled and Qwen3.8-27B defaults to xhigh effort). The 2026 question count and token sizes are unknown; this is a parametric grid, not a measurement.

conclusion: Two regimes, not one. (1) Text-only short-context surfaces, exemplified by LiveBench Instruction Following (about 1.8k input tokens per question): the bar (Opus 5.5 = 65.7) is exceeded on the official leaderboard by at least ten open-weights models (up to 77.1), three of which (Qwen3.8 27B 72.7, GLM-5.3 69.3, DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 67.7) map to Cloudflare Workers AI IDs; a pass costs 0.8 to 44.6 days of the free allocation or $0.09 to $4.90 paid (P14), and the scorer, adapter and ID-set preflight are already independently verified in the repo. The missing elements are a generator route and a Brain-owned operative configuration, not money or capability. (2) Agentic long-horizon surfaces (TB4, TB-Science, AutomationBench-scale): the free allocation is 1.5 to 4 orders of magnitude below one pass (P6), and measured open-weights gaps are about 14.3 points (FrontierCode) and 24.6 points (TB4) (P7, P8); the lever there is budget plus a demonstrated configuration uplift (P12). GitHub Models is retired (P1). See correction_notice for what the earlier version got wrong.
proposed_stage_gate_for_owner_reconcilia: S0 (zero spend; partly done in P10/P11): read the per-model pages to learn which candidate IDs require Workers Paid and which are version-pinned, and check semantic (not only name) disjointness of Terminal-Bench 2.1 from the exposed TB4 ledger using metadata only.
S1a (micro-pilot, owner-set hard cap; priced in P12): 12 trials on a few Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks to measure tokens per trial, per-task variance and harness failure modes before sizing S1b.

S1b (bounded budget B, cap set by the owner after S1a): run the raw pinned substrate and the Brain-configured system on the same non-frozen development tasks (the public Terminal-Bench 2.1 set, name-disjoint from the frozen TB4 tasks per P11) and estimate the configuration uplift with a confidence interval.
S2 (only if projected uplift is at least the residual in P7/P8): authorize frozen runs under the existing one-shot lease rules; otherwise record the predicate as unattainable on this substrate.

correction_notice: The first version of this receipt headlined 'the decisive lever is the $0 rule' and applied the AA-Briefcase token scale (52M to 970M tokens per pass) and the TB4/FrontierCode residuals to all four third-party-runnable bars. For LiveBench Instruction Following that was wrong: a pass is about 0.4M tokens and open-weights models already exceed the bar (P13, P14). Regime 2 below (agentic surfaces) keeps the original analysis; regime 1 (text-only surfaces) is new. Later in this PR a further correction was made in the public-bar receipt: AUTOMATIONBENCH_GE_40 compares a private-set bar to a public-set run (defect_findings).

reconciliation.question: What is the shortest verified path from the current state to the terminal capability now?
reconciliation.answer: There is no verified path to the terminal conjunction. The shortest verified path to the first real predicate closure is LIVEBENCH_IF_GE_65_7: (1) bind a pinned generator route from the P13 candidates; (2) measure tokens per question and raw-versus-Brain-configured difference on non-frozen prompts (IFBench's public test prompts; same 58 checker types); (3) one-shot frozen run after global prewave admission; (4) scoring with LiveBench's own strict mean-of-two aggregator (the repo's declared prompt-level loose metric is not the leaderboard's; defect finding in the public-bar receipt), by the independently verified checkers.
